title: Octopus Server Flaw Lets Authenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code Through Malicious JSON
content_md: Octopus Deploy has disclosed a high-severity vulnerability in Octopus Server that could allow authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted JSON content to vulnerable environments or projects. Tracked as CVE-2026-101169, the flaw stems from insecure JSON deserialization in Octopus Server. An attacker must first possess an authenticated account with permission to edit an Environment or Project. Once granted those permissions, the attacker can supply malicious JSON for an affected object and trigger arbitrary code execution within the Octopus Server process. Octopus Server Flaw The vulnerability affects Octopus Server deployments running on Linux and Microsoft Windows. Octopus Deploy discovered the issue on September 4, 2026, released patches on September 14, and published advisory 2026-10 on September 29. The company assigned the issue a High severity rating under its internal vulnerability-severity framework. While exploitation requires authentication and specific editing privileges, successful code execution in the server process could let an attacker tamper with deployment configuration, access sensitive deployment data, disrupt release automation, or potentially use the compromised server as a pivot point into connected environments. Octopus Server commonly orchestrates software deployments, manages project lifecycles, and stores sensitive configuration data.
